meta.description: Single source of truth for all Noble Architecture standard indexed face materials and their PBR render settings. Used by SketchUp plugins (GLB exporter, Window Configurator) and the TrueVision3D WebApp renderer for dynamic material lookup and swapping.
meta.namingConvention: SketchUpName must match the SketchUp material display_name exactly. Format: MAT{NNN}__{Category}__{Variant}. The prefix MAT + 3 digits + __ is required for the lookup system to recognise a material as indexed.
meta.exemptNote: MAT000E__ materials export in EVERY mode (including no_materials / whitecard) but do NOT receive PBR enrichment from the library. Their colour and opacity come from the SketchUp material itself -- the GLB exporter writes the Materials tray Opacity slider as baseColorFactor alpha + alphaMode BLEND -- and ValeVision3D PureEngine exempts them from the opaque whitecard replacement. An exempt material MAY still be catalogued here (see MAT105__GenericGlass__WhitecardTranslucent) so plugins can discover and create it; in that case the entry is a reference recipe for building the SketchUp material, not a set of render-time overrides.
meta.isExemptNote: IsExempt: true marks a catalogued material whose SketchUpName carries the MAT000E__ exempt prefix. Plugins should create it from the values here, then let the SketchUp material drive colour and opacity downstream.
meta.nprSeriesNote: MAT200__PainterlyNprSeries__ (30-Oct-2026) holds one swatch for every material class in PainterlyNPR's material library (Na__PainterlyNPR 07__Data__MaterialRecipes/PainterlyNPR__MaterialLibrary__Register__.json; the classes themselves are its 13__Scene__MaterialClasses), for painting a SketchUp model that ValeVision AURA draws in pen and wash. A different workflow from every other series, so every one is exempt: SketchUpName MAT000E__Npr__<NprClassKey> exports in every mode, whitecard included, with its own colour, and the class key stays readable in the GLB builder's <tag>::<material> node name. Catalogue key: MAT2 + the class Id in two digits (MAT202 is Brick); the sky (class 0) is not a material. BaseColor is the class's Albedo; NprClassKey, NprClassId, NprClassLabel and NprGroup (the register's group) are PainterlyNPR's own. Na PainterlyNPR Assets' Materials tab creates and paints them. Keep them out of ValeVision 3D and TrueVision presentation models: exempt, they are never whitecarded there.
meta.defaultMaterial: MAT001__Default is the reference template showing ALL possible keys with their default values. Other materials only need to specify keys that differ. Omitted keys inherit the default at render time.
meta.divergenceNote: No local material-library JSON copies remain. The old Window Configurator local copy (Na__AppConfig__MaterialsLibrary.json) was deleted in the Element Assembly Studio Pro v0.9.10 DataLib migration; Na__AssemblyStudio__AppData__MaterialManager__.rb now loads this centralised file live via Na__DataLib__CacheData. That module still hardcodes NA_SAFETY_GLASS_COLOR / NA_SAFETY_GLASS_ALPHA as a last-resort fallback for MAT101__GenericGlass when the library can't be loaded -- keep those two constants in sync with MAT101 here. The old ValeDesignSuite WindowPanelConfigurator (non-indexed 'natural-wood'/'glass' ComponentMaterial strings) is fully retired and no longer in use.

Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping.Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Purpose: Developer and agent reference mapping for translating SSOT material keys into SketchUp Ruby API material properties for SketchUp 2026.

Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Identit.SketchUpName: Sketchup::Materials#[] lookup key and Sketchup::Materials#add(name) create name. Also stored in Sketchup::Material#name.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Identit.Description: No direct Sketchup::Material description field. Store in material attribute dictionary metadata.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Identit.IsDefault: Loader control flag only. If true, skip material build entry.

Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__PbrFact.PbrRoughness: Sketchup::Material#roughness_factor= plus roughness_enabled= true when supported.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__PbrFact.PbrMetallic: Sketchup::Material#metallic_factor= plus metalness_enabled= true when supported.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__PbrFact.NormalScale: Sketchup::Material#normal_scale= and normal_enabled= true when a normal texture is assigned.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__PbrFact.OcclusionStrength: Sketchup::Material#ao_strength= and ao_enabled= true when an AO texture is assigned.

Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Texture.TextureMaps.EmissiveUrl: No direct Sketchup::Material emissive texture setter in Ruby API. Store as metadata for downstream renderer translation.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Texture.TextureMaps.AlphaUrl: No direct alpha-map setter in Sketchup::Material Ruby API. Store as metadata for downstream renderer translation.

Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.Transparent: Metadata only. SketchUp transparency behaviour is driven by alpha value and texture alpha.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.IsDoubleSided: Metadata only. Face side rendering is geometry/material assignment dependent, not a direct Sketchup::Material property.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.DepthWrite: Metadata only for downstream renderer translation.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.AlphaTest: Metadata only for downstream renderer translation.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.EnvMapIntensity: Metadata only for downstream renderer translation.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.EmissiveFactor: Metadata only for downstream renderer translation.
Na__DataLib__SketchUpApiMapping__Metadat.EmissiveIntensity: Metadata only for downstream renderer translation.

MAT101__GenericGlass.Description: Clear glass pane with a neutral grey tint

MAT105__GenericGlass__WhitecardTransluce.Description: Whitecard-safe translucent glazing -- the glass material that stays see-through under ValeVision PureEngine, where every indexed MAT###__ material is replaced by the opaque whitecard. Use it to subtly indicate a glazed element (balustrades, screens, juliet balconies, rooflights) in a whitecard model where a solid panel would hide the elevation behind it. Exempt by the MAT000E__ prefix on SketchUpName: it is never whitecarded, never SSOT-enriched at export, and renders identically under PureEngine and MaxEngine. Opacity travels from the SketchUp Materials tray slider into the GLB as baseColorFactor alpha + alphaMode BLEND, so the values below are the reference recipe for CREATING the material, not render-time overrides -- set the tray Opacity to 20 to match.

MAT801__SitePlan__WoodlandGreen.Description: Site plan face fill - woodland, hedges and planting. OPAQUE in SketchUp so the model reads while it is drawn; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency from SitePlan__FillOpacity in the Tags SSOT.

MAT802__SitePlan__WaterBlue.Description: Site plan face fill - ponds, lakes and watercourses (71__SitePlan__BaseMap__Waterbodies, with the Ponds & Lakes ripple) and still water - pools, formal ponds, water features (74__SitePlan__ExternalWorks__StillWater, the same blue with no ripple). Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency.

MAT803__SitePlan__ProposalRed.Description: Site plan face fill - the proposal, both new construction and alterations. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision washes it back to rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.1) from SitePlan__FillOpacity.

MAT804__SitePlan__GrasslandGreen.Description: Site plan face fill - fields, paddocks, lawns and open grass (75__SitePlan__SoftLandscape__Grassland). Sampled from the OS reference sheet's Grassland swatch: lighter and yellower than the woodland wash, so a field reads apart from a wood before its tufts are seen. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency.

MAT805__SitePlan__RoughGrasslandOlive.Description: Site plan face fill - rough grass, tussock, field margins and uncut verges (75__SitePlan__SoftLandscape__RoughGrassland). Sampled from the OS reference sheet's Rough grassland swatch: an olive grey, duller than Grassland beside it. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency.

MAT806__SitePlan__HardStandingGrey.Description: Site plan face fill - hard standing and paved driveways: drives, parking courts, yards and turning heads (74__SitePlan__ExternalWorks__HardStandingAndDriveways, 73__SitePlan__SiteFeature__Access, 74__SitePlan__ExternalWorks__HardSurfaces). A very light NEUTRAL grey, about 11 percent - the darker of the two hard standing greys, so a drive reads as tarmac beside the stone of MAT807 and still survives a laser printer. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency.

MAT808__SitePlan__NewPlantingWoodlandGre.Description: Site plan new planting woodland wash: the existing woodland green lightened approximately 20 percent towards white. Uses the existing Mixed Woodland tree pattern.

MAT809__SitePlan__DeckingBrown.Description: Site plan decking fill: pale warm grey-brown, lightened to sit quietly beside paving and planting. Solid warm grey-brown wash with the Hard Surfaces outline settings and no hatch.

MAT810__SitePlan__GravelStone.Description: Site plan gravel driveway fill: light warm stone RGB 230, 224, 212, beneath the sparse Gravel hatch. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision reads the tag fill opacity.

MAT807__SitePlan__PavingGrey.Description: Site plan face fill - paths and paving: footpaths, patios, terraces and paved areas (74__SitePlan__ExternalWorks__PathsAndPaving, 73__SitePlan__SiteFeature__Paths). A very light WARM grey, about 6 percent - the lighter of the two hard standing greys and a touch warm, so paving reads as stone beside the neutral drive (MAT806) rather than as the same surface a shade paler. Opaque in SketchUp; TrueVision applies the drawing transparency.

MAT901__Entourage__Silhouette__MidGrey.Description: Entourage silhouette fill -- flat mid grey at 50% opacity for fill-only camera-follow billboards (60_03xx__SceneEntourage__SilhouettePerson__*). Paint the faces, not the component. Matte, non-reflective, double-sided, no depth write, AO and profile-line excluded. Rendered from this entry by ValeVision MaxEngine (needs a __MaxModel Cloud Sync export); whitecard exports and PureEngine replace it with the whitecard like every indexed material.
